messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: na.value of gradient scales
parts:
Hi everyone,
There is an argument to scale_*_gradient* named "na.value" that allows you to set the color for na.values, or in my particular use, values outside the limits I have set using the limits argument. I am looking for and not seeing a way to set the values above the upper limit one color and the values below the lower limit a different color.

df <- data.frame(A = 1:50, B = 1:50, C = sample(1:10, 50, TRUE))
ggplot(df, aes(A, B, color = C)) + geom_point() + scale_color_gradient2(limits = c(4,6), na.value = "red")

In this example I made all outliers red, but suppose I want to ones above to be red and the ones below to be green. Any way of doing that?

Thanks,
Doug

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: na.value of gradient scales
parts:
Hi Doug,

Well, you can sort of do it like 

ggplot(df, aes(A, B)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = C)) +
    geom_point(color="red", data=subset(df, C < 4)) +
    geom_point(color="green", data=subset(df, C > 6)) +
    scale_color_gradient2(limits = c(4,6), na.value = NA)


but it's not nice and there is no legend to tell what the red and green points mean. My suggestion is to use another aesthetic to highlight values that fall outside the range--something like

df$out <-""
df$out[df$C < 4] <- "low"
df$out[df$C > 6] <- "high"

ggplot(df, aes(A, B, color=C, shape=out)) +
    geom_point()


Best,
Ista
